title: Lizzie Martin
text:
Lizzie Martin
As a joint PhD candidate in the Department of Political Science and Annenberg School for Communication at the University of Pennsylvania, I study public policy as a question of communication, with a focus on the American bureaucracy and its relationship to public opinion. You can visit my UPenn page here. I expect to receive my PhD in December 2026.
I also hold an MA in statistics from the Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania, an MPA in public policy with a certificate in Global Health and Health Policy from the Princeton University School for Public and International Affairs, and an AB in public policy and creative writing from Princeton University. Through the American Political Science Association, I have been a Public Scholarship Fellow and an Institute for Civically Engaged Research Fellow.
Professionally, I have spent seven years in the U.S. federal government, primarily working on program and policy evaluation as a social scientist in the General Services Administration Office of Evaluation Sciences. I have also been a Presidential Management Fellow at the CDC and a Scholars in the Nation’s Service Initiative Fellow at the Department of State.

title: Teaching
text:
arXiv Preprint | Code
Over the centuries, I have devoted countless hours to deciphering and translating the ancient scripts and dialects of the various peoples of Middle-earth. My goal is to gain a deeper understanding of the cultures and histories of these peoples by studying their languages. Currently, I am working on a monograph that explores the linguistic roots of the Elvish languages. Through extensive research and analysis, I hope to shed light on the connections between the different dialects of Elvish and their origins. This project has been particularly challenging, as Elvish is a complex and nuanced language, but I am determined to see it through to completion.

section: The History of the War of the Ring
text:
The History of the War of the Ring

arXiv Preprint | Code
I am creating a comprehensive and detailed history of the conflict that goes beyond the surface-level events. By gathering information from a variety of sources, including my own memories, written accounts, and oral histories, I hope to shed new light on this important period in Middle-earth’s history and provide valuable insights into the motivations and actions of the various players involved.
